title: Ops sync: pager noise & SLO triage (scratch)
content:
Purpose: prep for weekly ops sync (Thu 10:00). Focus on SLO health, paging trends, actioning recent top incidents and quick-runbook fixes. Put together concise talking points and proposed mitigations to agree with oncall rota before rollout window.

Agenda (10m alloted, aim for 25m total):
- Quick SLO snapshot (2m): error budget remaining for text-gen / inference-v2 / embeddings through EOD 6/21.
- Paging trend highlights (5m): nightly spikes, flapping alerts, noisy 3xx/4xx bursts.
- Top incidents review (8m): summary + short-term mitigations.
- Runbook and alert tuning proposals (7m): debounce, severity remap, new synthetic checks.
- Action item capture and owners (3m).

SLO snapshot notes (to pull before meeting):
- Error budget (28d rolling):
  - inference-text-gen: 84% remaining (good) but 7 consecutive days of elevated tail latency.
  - api-routing: 62% remaining (at risk if current trend continues).
  - embeddings: 92% remaining.
- Key metric to surface live: 99th pct latency (tokenization->first-token) for p95/p99 windows last 6h and last 7d.
- Recent change that correlates: model-variant rollout (v12 -> v12-q4) 2026-06-13 02:00 UTC. Need to overlay rollout window with latency spike.

Paging trends (quick summary from last 14 days):
- Nightly spike (02:00-04:00 UTC) in failure-rate alerts tied to backup job collisions in us-east-1. Pattern: 2.5x baseline alert rate on Sundays and early Mondays.
- Flapping cache-miss alerts for cache-tier-3 after config flip on 6/10 (partial rollback applied 6/11). Still seeing reoccurrence ~3x/week.
- Noise contributors: low-severity 4xx bursts from internal health probes misconfigured after service mesh update.

Top incidents (short):
- Incident: 2026-06-13 model rollout latency burst
  - Summary: customers observed p99 latency jumps ~4x during and after variant rollout. Auto-scaling absorbed TPU pressure but latency persisted for prefix-heavy requests.
  - Immediate mitigation applied: rollback to v12-stable for 3% of traffic, increased autoscaler cooldowns, KV cache warmup script deployed.
  - Follow-ups: validate kernel selection heuristic for long-prefix sequences (ENG-2145), add canary traffic shaping, add synthetic prefix-heavy test.
- Incident: 2026-06-08 nightly backup collision (us-east-1)
  - Summary: bulk snapshot process increased disk IO causing degraded throughput for dedupe service, manifested as 5xx for low-traffic tenants and triggered high-priority pages.
  - Mitigations: shift backup windows, add IO throttle in snapshot job. Action: confirm throttle holds under load (JIRA-SRE-309).

Runbook/alert tuning proposals (concrete):
- Alert debounce: increase debounce for "cache-miss-rate" from 30s -> 180s and require sustained increase for 2 consecutive windows before paging. Rationale: flapping causes noise, does not correlate with customer visible errors in many cases.
- Severity remap: move some 4xx health-probe alerts to INFO unless accompanied by elevated 5xx rate or SLO breach.
- Synthetic checks: add prefix-heavy generation synthetic that runs every 5m and measures cold-start p99; tag as "canary-synthetic" and surface in dashboard.
- Paging rules: add runbook step to check recent deploys + rollout tags in routing service (common root cause for model-related latency).
- Postmortem hygiene: require initial timeline + hypothesis (1 pager) within 7d, full RCA within 30d for incidents with >20% error budget consumption.

Queries / dashboards to refresh before meeting (assign):
- p99-latency-by-model-and-variant (last 7d) -> Priya
- alert-flap-heatmap (hourly buckets last 14d) -> Jun
- error-budget-consumption-by-service (28d) -> Maya
- synthetic-canary-success-rate (last 48h) -> Liam

Draft talking points (keep short):
- "We have headroom on most SLOs but two risk patterns: sustained p99 latency after model variant rollouts and noisy alerts from non-customer-facing probes. Need to prioritize quick runbook changes to reduce paging fatigue while we collect deeper telemetry."
- "Short-term: debounce and severity remap to reduce noise. Medium-term: add canary synthetic + improve kernel selection tests before rollout. Long-term: integrate rollout-aware guardrails in smart-routing."

Risks / questions for sync:
- Any objection to increasing debounce for cache-miss alerts? Potential downside: slower detection for real cache failures. Propose: implement debounce + amplify 5xx-linked alarms (two-tier).
- Do we want to gate variant rollouts behind synthetic p99 threshold? Can product accept the added rollout friction?

Action items (capture during sync):
- Maya: run error-budget refresh and paste top-5 tenant impacts in chat (due EOD 6/21).
- Priya: refresh p99-by-variant dashboard and confirm if v12-q4 shows systematic diff (due before sync).
- Jun: implement alert-debounce PR for cache-miss alert, start with staging rollout (due 6/24).
- Liam: add prefix-heavy synthetic (initial implementation) and hook to canary dashboard (due 6/25).
- All: agree on postmortem template update and timeline enforcement (sync ops owners 6/23).

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts:
- Consider moving some low-noise agents to slack threads instead of pages (stub a policy).
- Might be worth a short "oncall ergonomics" session next quarter to address sustained burnout signals.
- Remember to cross-check with product for rollout gating — don't overpromise developer friction improvements without product buy-in.

Meeting prep checklist (quick):
- [ ] Pull latest SLO numbers (Maya)
- [ ] Refresh p99 dashboards (Priya)
- [ ] Generate alert-flap heatmap (Jun)
- [ ] Draft debounce PR and link (Jun)
- [ ] Draft synthetic test code snippet (Liam)

-- end scratch --
